title: "CanadaLogin Signal Check"
subtitle: "For the two-week period of November 2 to 15"
author: "EDCP Data and Research Team"  # colin.douglas@cds-snc.ca
date: "2026-11-16"
params:
  edition: 11
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
    theme: [cosmo, _fonts.scss]   # _fonts.scss: self-hosted brand fonts
    toc: false

execute:

---

```{r setup}
# Queries are frozen to the November 2 - 15, 2026 period.
source("../R/connection.R")
source("../R/branding.R")
source("../R/colours.R")
source("../R/publishing.R")
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(dbplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(scales)
})

con <- connect_athena()

# Watermark date: the date this report is first created.
report_date <- as.Date("2026-11-16")

period_start <- as.Date("2026-11-02")
period_end <- as.Date("2026-11-15")

# Monday of the launch week; the service went live Apr 22.
series_start <- as.Date("2026-04-20")

# Figure 3 reads the weekdays of the last four weeks.
load_start <- as.Date("2026-10-19")

# Remembrance Day, a federal holiday, so not a typical weekday. It also had an
# unusual share of failed authentications.
remembrance_day <- as.Date("2026-11-11")

prev_start <- period_start - 14
prev_end <- period_start - 1

# An event's time as an Eastern Time timestamp. `time` is a UTC string.
et_time <- sql(paste(
  "with_timezone(CAST(substr(time, 1, 19) AS timestamp), 'UTC')",
  "AT TIME ZONE 'America/Toronto'"
))

# The relying-party registry, one row per application name. Several names map to
# one service, so aggregate after joining this.
relying_parties <- load_relying_parties(con) |>
  distinct(application_name, service_name, is_internal, launch_date) |>
  mutate(launch_date = as.Date(launch_date))

# Figure 1 --------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Weekly SSO events by public service, per the cookbook's sign-ins-by-application
# recipe. The period's four busiest are named; the rest are one grey band.
app_daily <- tbl(
  con, in_schema("ibm_verify_events_transformed", "events_app_login_counts")
) |>
  filter(
    as.Date(from_date) >= series_start, as.Date(from_date) <= period_end
  ) |>
  group_by(application_name, day = as.Date(from_date)) |>
  summarise(sso_events = sum(total_logins, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  collect() |>
  mutate(day = as.Date(day), sso_events = as.double(sso_events)) |>
  # A name with no registry row keeps its own name rather than dropping out.
  left_join(relying_parties, by = "application_name") |>
  filter(!coalesce(is_internal, FALSE)) |>
  mutate(service_name = coalesce(service_name, application_name))

period_ranking <- app_daily |>
  filter(day >= period_start, day <= period_end) |>
  group_by(service_name) |>
  summarise(sso_events = sum(sso_events), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(sso_events))

highlighted <- head(period_ranking$service_name, 4)

weekly_sso <- app_daily |>
  mutate(
    week_end = monday_of(day) + 6,
    service_group = if_else(
      service_name %in% highlighted, service_name, "Other services"
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(week_end, service_group) |>
  summarise(sso_events = sum(sso_events), .groups = "drop") |>
  # The first level stacks on top, so the grey band caps each bar.
  mutate(service_group = factor(
    service_group, levels = c("Other services", rev(highlighted))
  ))

period_sso <- sum(period_ranking$sso_events)
prev_sso <- app_daily |>
  filter(day >= prev_start, day <= prev_end) |>
  summarise(n = sum(sso_events)) |>
  pull(n)

public_service_count <- relying_parties |>
  filter(!is_internal, launch_date <= period_end) |>
  distinct(service_name) |>
  nrow()

top_share <- period_ranking$sso_events[1] / period_sso
second_share <- period_ranking$sso_events[2] / period_sso

# Figure 2 --------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Share of users who have signed in to two or more public services since launch.
# Counted by service, so MyCGC's two applications count once; pre-launch testing is out.
public_aliases <- tbl(con, in_schema("rp", "alias")) |>
  inner_join(tbl(con, in_schema("rp", "service")), by = "rp_id") |>
  filter(!is_internal) |>
  distinct(applicationname = alias, service_name = service_name_en, launch_date)

first_use <- tbl(con, in_schema("ibm_verify_events_raw", "application_usage")) |>
  filter(
    result == "success",
    !is.na(userid), userid != "", userid != "UNKNOWN"
  ) |>
  mutate(et_day = sql(paste0("date(", et_time, ")"))) |>
  filter(et_day <= period_end) |>
  inner_join(public_aliases, by = "applicationname") |>
  filter(et_day >= as.Date(launch_date)) |>
  group_by(userid, service_name) |>
  summarise(first_day = min(et_day, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  collect() |>
  mutate(first_day = as.Date(first_day))

# The day each user first reached one public service, and a second one.
user_reach <- first_use |>
  group_by(userid) |>
  arrange(first_day, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  summarise(
    services = n(),
    first_service_day = first(first_day),
    second_service_day = nth(first_day, 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

reach_weeks <- tibble(week_end = seq(series_start + 6, period_end, by = "week"))
reach_weekly <- reach_weeks |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    users = sum(user_reach$first_service_day <= week_end),
    multi_users = sum(user_reach$second_service_day <= week_end, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(multi_share = multi_users / users)

reach_latest <- slice_max(reach_weekly, week_end, n = 1)

# ATIP's two services joined on the same day, the start of the steep climb.
atip_launch <- relying_parties |>
  filter(!is_internal, startsWith(service_name, "ATIP")) |>
  pull(launch_date) |>
  min()

# The most common pair of services among users who reached two or more.
service_combos <- first_use |>
  filter(userid %in% user_reach$userid[user_reach$services >= 2]) |>
  group_by(userid) |>
  summarise(
    combo = paste(sort(service_name), collapse = " + "), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  count(combo, sort = TRUE)

# Figure 3 --------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Every IBM Verify event, all four raw tables, per second per 1,000 DAU in 15-minute
# ET bins. The Nov 4-6 surge of resent SMS OTP codes stays in, as real load.
load_days <- seq(load_start, period_end, by = "day")
load_days <- load_days[
  as.integer(format(load_days, "%u")) <= 5L & load_days != remembrance_day
]

# Partitions are UTC days, so read the day after the window for the ET evening.
raw_events <- function(table) {
  tbl(con, in_schema("ibm_verify_events_raw", table)) |>
    filter(
      .data$year == "2026",
      (.data$month == "10" & .data$day >= "19") |
        (.data$month == "11" & .data$day <= "16")
    ) |>
    mutate(et_ts = et_time) |>
    # hour() and minute() are Athena functions, passed through to SQL.
    mutate(
      et_day = as.Date(.data$et_ts),
      et_hour = hour(.data$et_ts), # nolint: object_usage_linter.
      et_minute = minute(.data$et_ts) # nolint: object_usage_linter.
    ) |>
    filter(.data$et_day %in% load_days)
}

event_tables <- c(
  "authentication_activity", "mfa_activity", "application_usage",
  "adaptive_access"
)

load_bins <- bind_rows(lapply(event_tables, \(table) {
  raw_events(table) |>
    mutate(bin = et_hour * 4L + floor(et_minute / 15L)) |>
    count(et_day, bin) |>
    collect()
})) |>
  mutate(et_day = as.Date(et_day), bin = as.integer(bin), n = as.double(n))

load_dau <- raw_events("authentication_activity") |>
  filter(!is.na(subject), subject != "", subject != "UNKNOWN") |>
  group_by(et_day) |>
  summarise(dau = n_distinct(subject), .groups = "drop") |>
  collect() |>
  mutate(et_day = as.Date(et_day), dau = as.double(dau))

bin_seconds <- 15 * 60

# Each day's rate per bin, every bin present so quiet ones count as zero.
load_daily <- load_bins |>
  group_by(et_day, bin) |>
  summarise(events = sum(n), .groups = "drop") |>
  complete(et_day, bin = 0:95, fill = list(events = 0)) |>
  inner_join(load_dau, by = "et_day") |>
  mutate(
    hour = bin / 4,
    rate = events / bin_seconds / dau * 1000
  )

load_typical <- load_daily |>
  group_by(hour) |>
  summarise(rate = median(rate), .groups = "drop")

load_peak <- slice_max(load_typical, rate, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)

# The median weekday also has a smaller late-morning peak.
morning_peak <- load_typical |>
  filter(hour >= 9, hour < 12) |>
  slice_max(rate, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
peak_labels <- bind_rows(morning_peak, load_peak)

# Events per DAU on the median weekday.
events_per_dau <- load_daily |>
  group_by(et_day) |>
  summarise(per_dau = sum(events) / first(dau), .groups = "drop") |>
  summarise(m = median(per_dau)) |>
  pull(m)

# A clock time as it reads in prose, "10:15 a.m."
format_clock <- function(hour) {
  h <- floor(hour)
  m <- round((hour - h) * 60)
  suffix <- if_else(h < 12, "a.m.", "p.m.")
  h12 <- if_else(h %% 12 == 0, 12, h %% 12)
  paste0(h12, ":", sprintf("%02d", m), " ", suffix)
}
```

Welcome to **CanadaLogin Signal Check**, a biweekly non-technical read on
CanadaLogin activity. This edition covers three topics: which online services
are driving CanadaLogin's traffic, how many users have used CanadaLogin to sign
in to more than one service, and when CanadaLogin is the busiest.

**ATIP's request service and GC Digital Talent carry most of CanadaLogin's
traffic.** Of the `r comma(period_sso)` SSO events in the last two weeks,
each one a signed-in user reaching an online service, the ATIP Online Request
Service had **`r percent(top_share, accuracy = 1)`** and GC Digital Talent
**`r percent(second_share, accuracy = 1)`**. The other
`r public_service_count - 2` online services shared the rest. Total traffic
held steady, against `r comma(prev_sso)` in the two weeks before.

```{r sso-by-service}
#| fig-height: 4.4
#| fig-alt: |
#|   Stacked bar chart of weekly SSO events by online service from the April
#|   2026 launch to November 15. Volume grows from June and jumps when ATIP
#|   joins in September. The last two weeks, shaded, hold steady at about
#|   16,000 a week. The ATIP Online Request Service is more than half of each
#|   of those bars, and GC Digital Talent the next largest.
# One colour per service, matching earlier editions.
service_colours <- c(
  "ATIP Online Request Service" = unname(colors$brand["orange"]),
  "GC Digital Talent" = unname(colors$brand["blue"]),
  "ATIP Online Management Tools" = unname(colors$brand["yellow"]),
  "IRIS" = unname(colors$brand["forest"]),
  "Other services" = unname(colors$greyscale[3])
)

# Shades the two period bars, each 6 days wide around its Sunday.
sso_plot <- ggplot(weekly_sso, aes(week_end, sso_events, fill = service_group)) +
  annotate(
    "rect", xmin = period_start + 2.5, xmax = period_end + 3.5,
    ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = colors$greyscale[5]
  ) +
  geom_col(width = 6) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = service_colours,
    breaks = c(highlighted, "Other services"),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = comma, limits = c(0, NA),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.06))
  ) +
  scale_x_date(
    breaks = seq(series_start + 6, period_end, by = "week"),
    date_labels = "%b %d"
  ) +
  theme_cds() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.justification = "left",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "SSO events in the week",
    title = "Most traffic goes to ATIP's request service and GC Digital Talent",
    subtitle = "SSO events per week by online service since the April 2026 launch."
  )

# Taller figure, so the logo height fraction is scaled to match the others.
add_cds_logo(
  add_watermark(sso_plot, date = report_date, edition = params$edition),
  height = 0.13 * 3.4 / 4.4
)
```

**About 1 in 100 users has used CanadaLogin for more than one service.** One
account for many services is one of CanadaLogin's main benefits to users, and
we have tried to measure it before. Until now, CanadaLogin's own internal
components, like the Manage and Migration apps, clouded the count. The new IBM
Verify event stream records every event rather than daily totals, so we can
now leave them out. Of the **`r comma(reach_latest$users)`** users who have
used CanadaLogin to sign in to an online service,
**`r comma(reach_latest$multi_users)`** have signed in to two or more. That
share has grown steadily since ATIP joined on `r format_long_date(atip_launch)`,
and the most common pair is ATIP's two services, at
`r service_combos$n[1]` users.

```{r multi-service-users}
#| fig-alt: |
#|   Line chart of the share of users who have used CanadaLogin to sign in to
#|   two or more online services since launch, by week from April to November
#|   15, 2026. It stays under 0.2% until ATIP joins on September 2, then climbs
#|   steadily to 1.1%.
reach_plot <- ggplot(reach_weekly, aes(week_end, multi_share)) +
  geom_line(colour = colors$brand["blue"], linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = reach_latest, colour = colors$brand["red"], size = 3) +
  geom_text(
    data = reach_latest,
    aes(label = percent(multi_share, accuracy = 0.1)),
    colour = colors$brand["red"], vjust = -1, fontface = "bold", size = 3.6
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = atip_launch, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey45",
    linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text", x = atip_launch + 2, y = Inf, hjust = 0, vjust = 1.5, size = 3.2,
    colour = "grey30",
    label = paste0("ATIP joins, ", format_long_date(atip_launch))
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = label_percent(accuracy = 0.1), limits = c(0, NA),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))
  ) +
  scale_x_date(
    breaks = seq(series_start + 6, period_end, by = "week"),
    date_labels = "%b %d"
  ) +
  theme_cds() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Share of users",
    title = "About 1 in 100 users has used CanadaLogin for two or more services",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Share of users who have signed in to two or more online services ",
      "since launch."
    )
  )

add_cds_logo(add_watermark(reach_plot, date = report_date,
                           edition = params$edition))
```

**CanadaLogin is busiest from mid-morning to mid-afternoon.** On a median
weekday, activity peaks around `r format_clock(morning_peak$hour)` and again
at `r format_clock(load_peak$hour)`, Eastern time
([America/Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tz_database_time_zones)).
The higher peak reaches
**`r number(load_peak$rate, accuracy = 0.01)` events per second for every
1,000 daily active users**. That ratio lets us plan for growth: a service
that brings 10,000 daily users would add about
`r number(load_peak$rate * 10, accuracy = 0.1)` events per second at the peak.
Events here count everything IBM Verify records: sign-ins, MFA codes, SSO
events and risk checks, including internal use. A typical user creates about
`r round(events_per_dau)` a day. These are events, not the "transactions" IBM
uses to measure service capacity, and each event produces multiple
transactions.

```{r load-by-time-of-day}
#| fig-height: 3.8
#| fig-alt: |
#|   Line chart of IBM Verify events per second per 1,000 daily active users
#|   by time of day, Eastern time, for each weekday of the past month (grey)
#|   and the median weekday (blue). The median rises from 7 a.m., peaks at 0.31
#|   at 10:45 a.m. and at 0.32 at 1:30 p.m. Two grey days spike near 6 a.m.
#|   during a surge of SMS codes.
hour_breaks <- seq(0, 24, by = 3)
hour_labels <- c(
  "12 a.m.", "3 a.m.", "6 a.m.", "9 a.m.", "12 p.m.", "3 p.m.", "6 p.m.",
  "9 p.m.", "12 a.m."
)

# Just above the grey days through the working day.
peak_label_y <- max(load_daily$rate[load_daily$hour >= 9 & load_daily$hour < 16]) *
  1.1

# Each 15-minute bin is drawn at its midpoint.
load_plot <- ggplot(load_daily, aes(hour + 0.125, rate)) +
  geom_line(
    aes(group = et_day),
    colour = colors$greyscale[4], linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = load_typical, colour = colors$brand["blue"], linewidth = 1.1
  ) +
  # Labels sit above the grey days on leaders, morning left and afternoon right.
  geom_segment(
    data = peak_labels,
    aes(x = hour + 0.125, xend = hour + 0.125, y = rate, yend = peak_label_y),
    colour = colors$brand["red"], linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  # Semi-transparent, so the median line shows through.
  geom_point(
    data = peak_labels, colour = colors$brand["red"], size = 3, alpha = 0.45
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = peak_labels,
    aes(
      y = peak_label_y,
      label = paste0(format_clock(hour), ": ", number(rate, accuracy = 0.01)),
      hjust = c(1.05, -0.05)
    ),
    colour = colors$brand["red"], fontface = "bold", size = 3.4
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = hour_breaks, labels = hour_labels, limits = c(0, 24),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  theme_cds() +
  # Room on the right for the last "12 a.m." label.
  theme(plot.margin = margin(5.5, 16, 5.5, 5.5)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time of day (ET)", y = "Events per second\nper 1,000 DAU",
    title = "CanadaLogin is busiest from mid-morning to mid-afternoon",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "IBM Verify events. Median weekday (blue) and each weekday of the past ",
      "month (grey)."
    )
  )

# Taller figure, so the logo height fraction is scaled to match the others.
add_cds_logo(
  add_watermark(load_plot, date = report_date, edition = params$edition),
  height = 0.13 * 3.4 / 3.8
)
```
